topics.label: Lecture opening and overview
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic welcomes students, connects the lecture to earlier practicals, and previews its learning outcomes.

topics.label: Tumor viruses and the discovery of cellular oncogenes
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how tumor-virus research led from the idea of transmissible cancers to the discovery that viruses can capture cellular proto-oncogenes.

topics.label: Experimental assays of cellular transformation
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how researchers test whether genes or mutations can give cells transformed properties.

topics.label: Functional classification of cancer genes and mutations
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the terms used to classify cancer mutations by their effects on tumor growth and cellular maintenance.

topics.label: Tumor-suppressor pathway disruption and mutation-specific effects
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics show how changes to RB-regulated cell-cycle control and mutation-specific effects on p53 can impair tumor-suppressive function.

topics.label: Genetic instability and its cellular causes and consequences
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how failures to maintain genome integrity generate genetic instability and affect cancer cells.

topics.label: Mutation timing in colorectal cancer progression
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines when mutations arise during colorectal tumor progression and how their order can affect its pace.

topics.label: Hereditary cancer predisposition
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how inherited mutations in caretaker or gatekeeper genes increase cancer risk and describes examples of hereditary cancer syndromes.

topics.label: Genetic instability is not required for malignancy
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic uses BRCA2 restoration during treatment to show that a cancer can remain lethal even after genetic instability is reduced.

topics.label: Lecture close and further reading
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic closes the lecture, invites questions, recommends reading, and previews the next lecture.
